title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: Hold: the credit-allocation API example omits the request body needed to select an environment, allocate credits and disable tenant-pool draw. The checklist also asks makers to evaluate every node although evaluations are documented only for new inline agents.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an agent that can reason, call tools and read knowledge before returning a result.

claims.claim: The credit-allocation screen is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Licensing.
Under Products, select Copilot Studio.
Select Manage Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The printed PUT URL with parenthetical entitlement and enforcement-rule names is a sufficient call to configure allocation and tenant-pool draw.
claims.fix: Keep PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01, but replace the parenthetical text with the required JSON body: {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment ID>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":5000},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":false}]}]}. Identify 5000 as an example allocation and require authenticated authorization and Content-Type: application/json, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity role.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through an environment's linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents, including inline agents.
claims.quote:
These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.
To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern supported certified connectors and permit MCP server-level blocking.

claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported. They're planned as a separate rule type in the future. For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic data policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ACP runtime evaluation uses the effective policy of the hosting environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
